label: NOTE: what this set reaches, and the claim it exists for
why: The set below reaches V92CP::infoToBits, 1,916 bytes and the largest single member of the class.  A GREEN t_v92info says our reading and the object agree; these say the reading is TIGHT.  THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST is 'char_02 is re-read for the thirteen bits at 36': the object shifts one register across the branch at .text+0x4ed10 and never reloads +0x002, so those thirteen entries are a signed byte's sign extension.  A version that re-read the field is identical for char_02 = 0 and for char_02 = -1 -- both give thirteen equal entries -- and differs the moment a bit below five is set, which is why four cases in t_v92info.cpp carry 0x0f, 0x01, 0x7f and -16.  SECOND is the fltTable_2 entry: the object's table has no 2^-8 and holds 2^-9 twice, so a generator reproduces the wrong weights and only a magnitude small enough to reach entry ten can tell.  WHAT NO ENTRY HERE REACHES: bitsPerSymbol = 0, which divides by zero on both sides; word_10c above six, which walks past both mask blocks (docs/deviations.md D570); and a NaN in any float, whose two sign forms disagree under -mno-ieee-fp.  All three are out of the grid on purpose, and a mutation of them would measure our own undefined behaviour rather than the object.
